title: Blue Film (HKLGFF 2026)
synopsis:
Edinburgh International Film Festival
Athens International Film Festival

 

Hong Kong Premiere

 

In a rented Los Angeles house, two men strip away their personas in a relentless, unnerving battle of words. Aaron Eagle, a swaggering young findom camboy, accepts $50,000 to entertain a masked, camera-wielding client. But this stranger knows too much, and as the mask comes off, the night turns into a reckoning neither man may survive intact. What follows is a claustrophobic two-hander that refuses every easy handhold, forcing its audience to sit with shame, complicity and the discomfiting humanity of people we would rather look away from. Tony winner Reed Birney and the beguiling Kieron Moore (BOOTS) give fearless, vanity-free performances in writer-director Elliot Tuttle's incendiary 85-minute debut, lit in spectral Yves Klein blue. Passed over by Sundance and SXSW, BLUE FILM is a provocation on the morality of desire that no audience will leave quietly.
